# Technical Static Document Generator

> A documentation engine that compiles to exactly one standalone `dist/index.html`, runnable from
> `file://` with zero network requests. Svelte 5 runes + MDsveX + Vite + Tailwind 4 + DaisyUI 5.
> This file is the authoring contract for LLM agents working in this repository: how to add a
> document, which components exist and what they take, how a diagram spec is written, and how to
> verify your work. Read this instead of touring `src/`.

The single rule everything else bends to: **no network at runtime.** No CDN, no web fonts, no runtime
fetches, no hosted services. A change that needs one of those is the wrong change.

## Commands

```bash
bun install
bun run dev              # vite dev server
bun run build            # → dist/index.html (single file, ~1.3 MB, gzip ~330 kB)
bun run preview
bun run check            # svelte-check — keep it at 0 errors, 0 warnings
bun run check:diagrams   # lint every diagram spec in src/content (exit 1 on structural errors)
```

After editing content or components, run `check`, `check:diagrams` and `build`. There is no test
suite; those three are the gate.

## Add a document

1. Create `src/content/NN-<id>.svx`. The stem after the numeric prefix is the document id:
   `03-deployment.svx` → `deployment`.
2. Add an entry to `src/config/sidebar.ts`, inside a `DocSection`:

```ts
{
  id: 'deployment',
  title: 'Deployment',
  description: 'One line, shown in search and the header',
  badge: 'v1.1',                      // optional
  loader: () => import('../content/03-deployment.svx'),
}
```

3. That is all. Search records, the on-this-page rail, prev/next and the sidebar are derived from
   that file plus that entry. The build warns when a content file has no sidebar entry.

Routes are `#/<docId>/<sectionSlug>`. Heading anchors come from `src/lib/slugify.ts`, which the
build-time index and the browser decorator both run over the same text — that shared function is the
only reason a search result's anchor matches the rendered heading. Keep it dependency-free.

## Authoring a page

`.svx` is markdown with components mixed in. The leading `#` heading is the document title. Data for
components is authored inline in a `<script lang="ts">` block as plain literals — there are no JSON
content files on purpose.

```svx
<script lang="ts">
  import Callout from '$components/Callout.svelte';
  import ArchitectureCanvas from '$components/ArchitectureCanvas.svelte';

  const nodes = [
    { id: 'api', title: 'Public API', subtitle: 'REST', type: 'backend' as const, x: 40, y: 50 },
  ];
</script>

# Deployment

<Callout type="warning" title="Air-gapped">No outbound calls at any point.</Callout>

<ArchitectureCanvas title="Runtime topology" nodes={nodes} />
```

Aliases: `$components` → `src/lib/components`, `$lib`, `$config`, `$content`.

Fenced code is highlighted at build time by Shiki with dual themes, so theme switching costs no
re-highlight. Shiki never reaches the client bundle. These transformer markers work inside a fence:

```ts
const legacy = false;   // [!code --]
const current = true;   // [!code ++]
const important = 1;    // [!code highlight]
```

### Editable codeblock placeholders

Code blocks automatically convert single-line `<identifier>` tokens (e.g. `<sales_key>`, `<tenant_id>`)
into interactive inline inputs at runtime. Users can fill in custom values and click **Copy** to
copy the entire code snippet with their values applied (or placeholder defaults if left blank).
Empty `<>` and multi-line patterns are ignored.

To disable placeholder decoration on a specific code snippet, add `data-placeholders="false"` or
`data-no-placeholders` to the `<pre>` or its `.code-block` wrapper.

## Components

Layout components (`LayoutShell`, `Router`, `SearchModal`, `TocRail`, `PageNav`, `ThemeSwitcher`,
`DiagramFrame`) are wired into the shell. Content components, with their exact props:

| Component | Props |
|---|---|
| `Callout` | `{ type?: 'info' \| 'warning' \| 'success' \| 'error' \| 'tip', title?, children }` |
| `Tabs` | `{ items: { id, label, language?, snippet? }[], activeId? }` |
| `ApiEndpoint` | `{ method, path, description?, requestBody?, curlExample?, responseExample? }` |
| `JsonTree` | `{ data: unknown, title?, defaultExpandedDepth? }` |
| `DataTable` | `{ columns, rows, rowKey?, caption?, empty?, sortKey?, sortDir?, density?, layout?, stickyFirst?, maxHeight?, stack?, wrap? }` |
| `MermaidDiagram` | `{ code: string, title? }` |
| `ArchitectureCanvas` | `{ title?, nodes, connections?, boundaries?, interactive? }` |
| `AdrViewer` | `{ records: { id, status: 'accepted' \| 'proposed' \| 'deprecated' \| 'superseded', date, title, context, decision, consequences? }[] }` |

A `DataTable` column is
`{ key, label, align?, sortable?, width?, cell?, badge?, grow?, priority?, numeric?, sortFn? }`.
Sizing has exactly one strategy per table, and both start from "the table fits its container":

- **`grow`** — a weight per column. Any column declaring one puts the table in a fixed layout where
  the weights are the only sizing input: each column gets a plain percentage, so the widths always
  add up to the container and a value too long for its column truncates instead of widening the
  table past the box it is in. A column without a weight takes one share; `width` and `priority`
  belong to the auto layout and are ignored here. Weight a column by what it needs, not by what it
  may take.
- **`priority: 2 | 3`** — drops the column below 34rem / 28rem of **container** width. Ignored in a
  fixed layout, where removing a cell would re-map every later column's width onto the wrong column.
  Use it for genuinely secondary columns; a column the reader needs is better off shrinking.

The table answers to its own box — the article measure, which the header's width toggle moves — and
never the viewport. Below 28rem each row becomes a card with every cell named, and the header row
survives as the sort bar so sorting stays reachable. `stickyFirst` and `maxHeight` are for tables
that genuinely scroll: one that fits has nothing to pin and nothing to stick.

Any scroll region — markdown tables and Shiki blocks included — gets an edge fade and keyboard
access from `src/lib/scroll-affordance.ts`. Components attach it with `use:scrollAffordance`; the
document decorator covers the markup no component owns.

`MermaidDiagram` renders with `securityLevel: 'strict'` and a token-derived theme. Add `accTitle:` and
`accDescr:` lines inside the mermaid source to describe the diagram for screen readers; the hint text
under the diagram tells the reader the same thing.

## Diagram specs

`ArchitectureCanvas` draws an authored topology. **Topology is authored, never solved** — there is no
layout engine, and the same spec always produces the same diagram. Nodes are placed by hand as canvas
percentages; everything else is derived from them.

```ts
const nodes = [
  { id: 'client', title: 'Local Browser', subtitle: 'file://', type: 'client', x: 15, y: 26, variant: 'emphasis' },
  { id: 'api', title: 'Public API', subtitle: 'REST', type: 'backend', x: 48, y: 26 },
];
const connections = [
  { from: 'client', to: 'api', label: 'HTTPS', fromSide: 'right', toSide: 'left' },
  { id: 'emit', from: 'build', to: 'client', label: 'Emits dist/index.html',
    fromSide: 'bottom', toSide: 'top', variant: 'emphasis', width: 2, via: [[48, 60]], labelAt: [48, 42] },
];
const boundaries = [
  { id: 'edge', kind: 'region', label: 'Edge', wraps: ['client'] },
  { id: 'trust', kind: 'security-group', label: 'No network', wraps: ['api'], pad: 22 },
];
```

### Node

`{ id, title, type?, variant?, subtitle?, tags?, highlight?, x, y }`

- `x` / `y` are percentages of the canvas and describe the node's **centre**.
- `type` picks icon and tone, and defaults to `service`:
  `client`, `gateway`, `service`, `database`, `security`, `cache`, `frontend`, `backend`, `cloud`,
  `messagebus`, `external`.
- `variant` is emphasis, independent of type: `default`, `emphasis`, `security`, `dashed`.
  `highlight: true` is the legacy alias for `variant: 'emphasis'`.

### Connection

`{ id?, from, to, label?, variant?, dashed?, bidirectional?, color?, fromSide?, toSide?, route?, via?, labelAt?, labelDx?, labelDy?, labelSegment?, width? }`

- **A side is a contract, not a hint**: `left | right | top | bottom`. The first and last segment run
  perpendicular to the side they leave and enter.
- `route`: `auto` (default) keeps the straight centre-to-centre line when no sides are authored, and
  routes orthogonally when they are. Also `straight`, `orthogonal-h`, `orthogonal-v`.
- `via` holds waypoints in canvas percentages and is how you steer a route around an obstacle.
- Label placement: `labelAt` (percentages), `labelDx` / `labelDy` (px nudge), `labelSegment`
  (zero-based segment of the route).
- `width` is clamped to 0.5–6 px; the default is 1.5. `color` is an escape hatch — prefer `variant`,
  which resolves through the theme.

### Boundary

`{ id, kind: 'region' | 'security-group', label, wraps: string[], pad? }`

The box is derived from the members' measured sizes. Only `pad` is authored, and it applies to the
sides and bottom: the top edge derives its own inset so the boundary's own label never collides with a
relationship label lifted clear of the first row.

### Invariants

These are checked, not suggestions. One obvious main path, and a side branch leaves the nearest
main-path node. Relationship labels are semantic data: reposition or shorten one, never delete it to
clear a collision. Spacing means clear gap, not centre distance.

`bun run check:diagrams` reports: duplicate or malformed ids, unknown endpoints, self-connections,
duplicate connections, boundaries that wrap nothing or enclose a node they do not claim, isolated
nodes, nodes closer than the 34 px clear gap the layout is tuned for, routes crossing an unrelated
box, routes crossing a boundary label, labels masking a node, and labels that merely restate their
endpoints. Structural problems are errors and fail the run; composition problems are warnings.

Structure is exact in the script, but its geometry uses estimated box sizes. The browser measures the
real ones and reports through `console.warn`, plus a badge and an overlay in the frame's toolbar. That
runtime pass runs in development, or whenever the URL carries `?diagram-debug` — which is the way in
when a dev server is started from a shell that exports `NODE_ENV=production`, where
`import.meta.env.DEV` is false.

### Export

The frame's export menu downloads a standalone SVG, a PNG, or copies the SVG source. Both are rebuilt
from the spec and the measured layout, not copied from the DOM, so an export never carries selection,
focus rings, pan/zoom state or the diagnostics overlay. The SVG export can embed both themes behind a
`prefers-color-scheme` query.

## Theme and token rules

`src/theme/tokens.css` is the only file to edit to change how the product looks. Components reference
only the declared vocabulary: `bg-base-100/200/300`, `text-base-content`, `border-edge`,
`border-edge-strong`, `rounded-chip` (3 px) / `rounded-edge` (4 px) / `rounded-panel` (6 px), and
`text-micro/meta/body/title`.

Banned inside `src/lib/**`: `rounded-2xl`, `rounded-3xl`, `border-base-content/N`, `text-[Npx]`,
literal hex, `bg-slate-*`.

```bash
grep -rnE 'rounded-(2xl|3xl)|border-base-content/|text-\[1[0-9]px\]' src/lib
```

- Adding a preset is a `@plugin "daisyui/theme"` block in `tokens.css` plus a row in
  `src/theme/presets.ts`. No component edits — if a component needs a change, the token layer is
  wrong.
- Dark mode keys off `data-color-scheme`, never the preset name, so renaming a preset cannot break a
  stylesheet.
- Renderers that cannot read a CSS variable (Mermaid, the SVG export) read resolved values through
  `readToken()` from `src/lib/css-tokens.ts`, with per-preset hex in the `--diagram-*` group.

## Accessibility

Treat it as a requirement, not a polish pass: colour is never the only signal (pair it with an icon,
a label or weight), interactive things are real `<button>` elements with accessible names, and there
are no `svelte-ignore a11y_*` suppressions anywhere in the tree.

## Gotchas

- **The search index strips components and expressions.** `vite-plugins/docs-index.ts` removes
  `<script>` blocks, component tags and `{…}` expressions before indexing, and keeps prose, headings
  and fenced code. So diagram node labels, ADR text and component props are *not* searchable — if
  something must be findable, say it in prose or a heading.
- **`src/lib/slugify.ts` is a contract.** It runs on both sides of the build; changing it changes
  every existing anchor.
- **Do not hand-tune derived geometry.** Node coordinates and route anchors are yours; boundary
  insets, label lanes, the fit and label lifting are the renderer's. If a diagram looks wrong, move a
  node, author a side or a waypoint, or read a diagnostic — do not add a constant.
- **`highlight` and `dashed` are legacy aliases.** Write `variant` in new specs.
- **No math functions in a `<col>` width.** A `calc()` or `max()` there is resolved once and then
  frozen at that pixel value, so the column stops answering to its container. `DataTable` emits plain
  percentages for exactly that reason.

## Where things live

```
src/content/*.svx           documents
src/config/sidebar.ts       navigation, doc metadata, loaders
src/config/site.ts          product name, badge, tagline
src/theme/tokens.css        the design tokens and the presets
src/theme/presets.ts        preset registry
src/lib/diagram/            diagram model, geometry, validator, palette, SVG export
src/lib/components/         content components + DiagramFrame
src/lib/layout/             shell, router, rails
vite-plugins/docs-index.ts  build-time search index
scripts/check-diagrams.ts   the diagram linter behind `bun run check:diagrams`
```
